First operation

Hold one total. Watch the categories move underneath it.

142,12 1/2

Source-facing monetary notation retained. The historical accounting labels are not modernized here.

Route A
107,50 + 34,62 1/2 = 142,12 1/2

The added amount sits on a meeting-labeled line. The exact meeting wording is not yet secure.

Source face: Back · lower accounting block

Route B
107,15 + 31,81 1/4 + 3,16 1/4 = 142,12 1/2

Tennessee, Illinois, and M. are visible on the sheet; their accounting roles are not settled.

Source face: Back · lower accounting block

What changed?

The base drops from 107,50 to 107,15: a difference of 0,35.

The added grouping increases by that same 0,35.

The total does not move. The classification does.

Derived from the two routes on the Back face

The paper supplies a bridge.

The lower block begins with a source-facing reading approximately “Of the Above 107, 2/4.” A following line reads strongly as “Value Communicated M. $107-15.” Because 2/4 equals one-half, the paper itself places 107,50 beside 107,15.

Source face: Back · lower accounting block

So what does Tennessee mean? What does Illinois mean?

They are visibly separate accounting labels in Route B. Their exact institutional job is still open. This prototype does not turn them into geography, donor origin, or jurisdiction without another source earning that move.

What is “M.”?

It recurs immediately before dollar amounts and belongs to the accounting notation. Its expansion remains open.

Why show the front face at all?

The front carries an accounting-method note beginning “When I made out this report…” and appears to say that the value of a collect-/collection category was handled separately. That may explain the reclassification visible on the back, but the exact wording is not secure enough to close the question. Use the Front and Close-up buttons to inspect it.

Source face: Front · method note; Close-up crosses the fold

Why is the front note transcribed cautiously?

An earlier reading treated it as “made a mistake.” Enlargement did not support that wording, so it was withdrawn. The present reading keeps the secure beginning and leaves the remaining words open.

Source face: Front · method note; checked against Close-up

Could another photograph change the reading?

Yes. The available front representations include an unsleeved photograph and a smaller photograph made through a plastic sleeve. The sleeve is not a complete barrier, but glare and softness can hide letter joins and small fractions. Even the unsleeved image does not settle every word. A new perpendicular, high-resolution, even-light detail—showing whole rows, the amount column, and one neighboring line above and below—could materially improve the index. It would be another representation of this same source face, not a second historical witness.

What can a person do next?

Return to the image. Find the carried total, then find the two bases. Ask what category moved, what stayed fixed, and which words on the sheet could explain that movement. Only then open neighboring sources.

Another entrance into the same historical sheet

The people on the paper.

The money was recorded alongside names and contributions in cloth. A name here may matter to a researcher whose question has nothing to do with this account's arithmetic or with Reverend Robert Bell. Search the occurrences, then go back to the marks.

Present limits.
The account's maker and precise beneficiary are unproved. “Charity Hall” is a collection association, not a manuscript attribution. These are named entries, not a verified headcount of donors. Nine readings are carried by the existing jacket and source-facing correction notes; fourteen back-face readings are newly provisional and await independent collation. No two matching surnames have been joined as people or relatives.

Unnamed person references · separately indexed

The manuscript sometimes refers to a person without supplying their name. These references do not increase the number of named occurrences above. The single entry below remains an uncollated source reading, not a child identified, counted as a donor, or assigned a proven relationship.

Each entry has its own occurrence ID, face and region, wording as provisionally read, and direct historical-source road. The CSV is an index to inspect and challenge, not a list of identified people. Identity comparison begins at source occurrence → candidate link → evidenced identification. These 23 entries are not the full sheet; source review may add, split, merge, or revise readings.

One unnamed person-reference phrase from B3 is now indexed separately; other unnamed or difficult-to-read rows remain unindexed. The names in this view are a small, correction-ready specimen—not a claim about the complete donor population. Several entries may reflect repeat contributors, and a label may represent a household, intermediary, or a person not yet identified.
